May contain spoilers from Sky King's Tomb **Source** [Pathfinder #193: Mantle of Gold](/Sources.aspx?ID=206) pg. 85 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** 1 --- This shield is grown entirely of specially treated fungi, giving it the appearance of a frilly disc.
When left atop at least 1 bulk of organic matter, it gains fast healing 1; after 10 minutes 1 Bulk of the organic matter has been consumed by the shield. This shield doubles its hardness against bludgeoning, electricity, and sonic damage. **Activate** manipulate; **Trigger** The shield is broken; **Effect** The shield spews spores into one adjacent square, dealing persistent poison damage to all creatures in within it; a successful Fortitude save negates the damage. **Craft Requirements** You are trained in Nature, and can cast a fungus spell or are fungus. Mycoweave Shield (Lesser) **Source** [Pathfinder #193: Mantle of Gold](/Sources.aspx?ID=206) pg. 85 **Price** 40 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The shield has Hardness 2, HP 12, and BT 6. When the shield breaks, the reaction deals 1d6 persistent poison damage with a DC 16 Fortitude saving throw. Mycoweave Shield (Greater) **Source** [Pathfinder #193: Mantle of Gold](/Sources.aspx?ID=206) pg. 85 **Price** 40 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The shield has Hardness 4, HP 64, and BT 32. When the shield breaks, the reaction deals 2d6 persistent poison damage with a DC 24 Fortitude saving throw. Mycoweave Shield (Major) **Source** [Pathfinder #193: Mantle of Gold](/Sources.aspx?ID=206) pg. 85 **Price** 40 gp **Bulk** 1 --- The shield has Hardness 6, HP 110, and BT 55. When the shield breaks, the reaction deals 3d6 persistent poison damage with a DC 35 Fortitude saving throw.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 20"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mythic Armor Potency](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3498)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 148

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This armor is etched with a mythical ward providing unparalleled defense. Increase the armor’s item bonus to AC by 4, and the armor can be etched with four [property runes](/Rules.aspx?ID=3168).

**Activate—Survive Devastation** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** An enemy critically succeeds against you with a weapon or unarmed [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306);  **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); if the triggering Strike was made by a mythic creature, it’s a normal success instead. If it was made by a non-mythic creature, it’s a failure.

**Craft Requirements** Mythic armor potency runes can only be crafted, etched, or transferred by a mythic character  capable of making a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check at mythic proficiency (such as by having the Artisan’s Calling).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Mythic Resilient](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3499)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 149

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto armor

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Mythic resilient runes imbue armor with unrivaled protection from a wide array of effects. The armor grants a +4 item bonus to saving throws to the wearer.

**Activate—Defy Obliteration** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You critically fail a saving throw;  **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320); if the triggering save was made due to an effect created by a mythic monster, hazard, or other effect, it’s a normal failure instead. If the save was made due to an effect that wasn’t mythic, it becomes a success.

**Craft Requirements** Mythic resilient runes can only be crafted, etched, or transferred by a mythic character capable of making a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check at mythic proficiency (such as by having the Artisan’s Calling).

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

>
[Mythic Striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3500)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 149

**Price** 70,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This weapon is filled with unmatched destructive power. The weapon deals five weapon damage dice.

**Activate—Unstoppable Devastation** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You roll the weapon damage dice for a [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306) with this weapon and do not like the result;  **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) and reroll your weapon damage dice, taking the higher of the two results.

**Craft Requirements** Mythic striking runes can only be crafted, etched, or transferred by a mythic character capable of making a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check at mythic proficiency (such as by having the Artisan’s Calling).

</column>

**Activate—Unerring Blow** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561))  **Trigger** You roll an attack roll to Strike with this weapon and receive a critical failure;  **Effect** Spend a [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3320) and reroll your attack roll with mythic proficiency, taking the higher of the two results.

**Craft Requirements** Mythic weapon potency runes can only be crafted, etched, or transferred by a mythic character capable of making a [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) check at mythic proficiency (such as by having the Artisan’s Calling).

[Navaratna of the Solar Ruby](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3480)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=537" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=579" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tian Xia Character Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=230) pg. 131

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

These nine flawless gems are set within a golden necklace, their centerpiece a holy ruby pulled from the center of a sun. So long as you are wearing the navaratna, you ignore all [environmental effects due to temperature](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820), do not take penalties due to [wind](/Rules.aspx?ID=2821), and ignore all damage and effects from droughts, [floods](/Rules.aspx?ID=2832), and [earthquakes](/Rules.aspx?ID=2828). You are also immune to damage from [starvation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2603). The navaratna does not otherwise grant you resistance against damage (such as [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=604) or [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) damage).

**Activate—Sutra of the Flawless Servant** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=612)) **Frequency** once per hour;; **Trigger** An ally within 30 feet fails a saving throw against an [temperature](/Rules.aspx?ID=2820) environmental effect;  **Effect** You offer a prayer for your divine protection to extend to your companion. The creature rerolls the triggering saving throw with a +2 item bonus. They must take the new result, even if it is worse.

**Destruction** The navaratna must be swallowed by a fiendish [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579) [lion](/Monsters.aspx?ID=2866); the lion must then by killed by drowning in a lake of [naga](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=446) venom and left to rot for a year. At the stroke of midnight on the final day, the artifact is destroyed.

**Requirement** You’re trained in Survival.

---

This jaunty feather is affixed to headgear and can guide you in times of trouble, twisting to point in different directions. When you activate the talisman, you roll the triggering >Survival check to Sense Direction or Track twice, and use the higher result.

For 24 hours, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival checks to Sense Direction, so long as you’re navigating toward the same destination as when you activated the talisman, and a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival checks to Track, so long as you continue to Track the same creature as when you activated the talisman. After 24 hours, the feather disintegrates, becoming mundane dust that blows away on the breeze.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 613

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This string of beads appears to be a hemp string with lustrous red beads of various sizes hanging from it. When activated, it briefly appears in its true form: a golden chain with golden spheres attached by fine threads.

 Numerous varieties of the _necklace of fireballs exist_. Each has a different basic Reflex save DC and includes a combination of spheres dealing different amounts of damage, as listed for each type below. When all the beads are gone, the necklace becomes a non-magical hemp string.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You detach a sphere from the necklace, causing it to glow with orange light. After you activate a sphere, if you or anyone else hurls it (an Interact action), it detonates as a [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119) where it lands. Your toss can place the center of the _fireball_ anywhere within 70 feet, though at the GM's discretion you might need to make an attack roll if the throw is unusually challenging. If no one hurls the sphere by the start of your next turn, it turns into a non-magical red bead.

---

This string of beads appears to be a hemp string with lustrous red beads of various sizes hanging from it. When activated, it briefly appears in its true form: a golden chain with golden spheres attached by fine threads.

 Numerous varieties of the _necklace of fireballs exist_. Each has a different basic Reflex save DC and includes a combination of spheres dealing different amounts of damage, as listed for each type below. When all the beads are gone, the necklace becomes a non-magical hemp string.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You detach a sphere from the necklace, causing it to glow with orange light. After you activate a sphere, if you or anyone else hurls it (an Interact action), it detonates as a [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119) where it lands. Your toss can place the center of the _fireball_ anywhere within 70 feet, though at the GM's discretion you might need to make an attack roll if the throw is unusually challenging. If no one hurls the sphere by the start of your next turn, it turns into a non-magical red bead.

This necklace strung with miniature stone throwing knives. As long as you wear it, you are never without a weapon, a crude surgical tool, or stake for a vampire, if necessary in following Pharasma’s teachings.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You pluck a miniature knife from the necklace, and it grows into a normal stone, steel, or wooden _[dagger](/Weapons.aspx?ID=3)_ for as long as you hold it, fading away 1 round after it leaves your hand. No matter how many knives you pull from the necklace, you never seem to deplete them. Wooden daggers from the necklace are as effective as ordinary steel daggers and can be useful to stake vampires.

**Source** [Gamemastery Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=22) pg. 91

**Usage** worn necklace

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

</column>

---

This beautiful necklace appears to be a magical item such as a [_necklace of fireballs_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=449) or a [_pendant of the occult_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=450). When invested, it magically locks in place, suspiciously tightly, and fuses to you. When you enter a situation of extreme stress (as determined by the GM), the necklace tightens around your neck, [suffocating](/Rules.aspx?ID=468) you and dealing 30 bludgeoning damage to you at the end of each of your turns. Once per round, you can spend a single action to attempt a DC 34 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check or Fortitude save; success means you don’t take the damage on your current turn, but you continue suffocating. The necklace loosens after you’ve been dead for a month.

</column>

May contain spoilers from Crown of the Kobold King **Source** [Crown of the Kobold King](/Sources.aspx?ID=148) pg. 116 **Price** 30 gp **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**Interact --- This potent necromantic serum is distilled from the body of an intelligent corporeal [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) who seeks to establish absolute control over their undead minions. The raw materials of a _necrobinding serum_ are composed of a slurry made from the creator's own flesh and blood mixed with pulped fungal toxins. The exact ingredients vary, but the act of brewing a _necrobinding serum_ is typically viewed with distaste at best and, in many societies, is regarded as an evil act. While _necrobinding serum_ isn't a poison, its method of delivery is identical to that of an injury poison—it's applied to a weapon that's then used to Strike an undead target (living creatures suffer no additional effect from exposure to a dose of _necrobinding serum_). When an undead creature is targeted by a dose of _necrobinding serum_, it must attempt a DC 19 Will save. **Critical Success** The undead creature is unaffected.
**Success** The undead creature is momentarily disoriented; it takes a –1 status penalty to all attack rolls made against you until the start of your next turn.
**Failure** The undead creature becomes [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18) toward you. If it was already friendly, it becomes [helpful](/Conditions.aspx?ID=21). It can't use [hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against you. This effect persists for 8 hours if the undead is [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108). Against other undead, the effect gains the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) trait and persists for 10 minutes.
**Critical Failure** The undead creature becomes helpful toward you and can't use hostile actions against you. This effect persists for 24 hours if the undead is mindless. Against other undead, the effect gains the mental trait and persists for 1 hour. **Craft Requirements** You must be a corporeal undead, and the serum must include some of your flesh and blood.

You can use this slimy, rotting mushroom as a [spell catalyst](/Rules.aspx?ID=1509) when you cast an [_acid grip_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1436) spell by tapping it against the target, causing the mushroom to release a cloud of necrotic spores. When you do, acid grip loses the [acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524) trait, gains the [fungus](/Traits.aspx?ID=614) trait, and all acid damage the spell deals becomes [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) damage. On a hit, the target additionally gains the [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) and [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) conditions, with the listed values, as the spores consume their flesh. As long as the target is taking [persistent void damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), they can’t reduce the value of their sickened condition below 1.

This thin, wand-like implement is carved from bone and scrimshawed with depictions of battle. While holding the needle of undeath, [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=652) [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creatures see you as one of their own and are [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=82) to you until you take [hostile actions](/Rules.aspx?ID=2251) against them, and you have a +2 item bonus to [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) and [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) checks against intelligent undead. This does not affect a summoned undead’s attitude.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Speak with Undead;  **Frequency** once per hour;   **Effect** You can use Diplomacy to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=2392) on mindless undead or make simple requests of them with a +2 item bonus. You cannot make this request of someone else’s summoned undead.

[Nemesis Name](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2213)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Tattoo" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=262" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 121

**Price** 650 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** tattooed on the body

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You want revenge badly enough that you tattoo your nemesis's name in a place you can easily see to remember your vow to settle the score. Anyone who sees the tattoo senses your hatred of the named being. Receiving a new _nemesis name_ makes any you already have non-magical.

You gain a +2 status bonus to damage rolls against the creature named on your tattoo, but this nemesis gains a +1 status bonus to damage rolls against you.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Frequency** once per round;  **Requirements** You can see your nemesis, and they're within 30 feet of you; **Effect** You focus your hatred into a mental scream. Your nemesis takes 3d6 mental damage, which they can resist with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) DC 26 Will save. You take half as much damage as your nemesis does, and you can't reduce this damage in any way.

</column>

Made of polished wood, a _neophyte's fipple_ is a block flute enchanted to guarantee melodic sound. When you Perform a song on the fipple to Activate it, your ability modifier, proficiency bonus, and item bonus for the Performance check total +7, regardless of what they would normally be. </title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Price** 1 gp

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

You can use a net either on its own or attached to a rope. When attached to a rope, you can use the net to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) a Medium or smaller creature up to 10 feet away (instead of only adjacent creatures). You can continue to Grapple to keep your hold on the target so long as the target remains within 10 feet and you continue to hold the net. The grabbed creature gains a +2 circumstance bonus to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) unless you are adjacent to them, and it can attempt a DC 16 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Force Open](/Actions.aspx?ID=34) the net entirely. Once the target is no longer [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20), the net is unwieldy until refolded with an Interact action with the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait that requires two hands; if used without being refolded, Grapple checks made with the net take a –2 penalty.

 When the net is unattached, you can attempt a ranged attack roll using your simple weapon proficiency against a Medium or smaller creature within 20 feet. On a hit, the target is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) and takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it Escapes, and on a critical hit, it's also immobilized until it Escapes. The Escape DC is 16. A creature adjacent to the target can Interact to remove the net.

---

This stick of dark-gray incense carries a faint, strange odor that’s different for any creature that smells it—mimicking a scent that evokes feelings of nostalgia or homesickness. You begin the activation of a stick of _netherwalk incense_ by lighting it on fire as a single Interact action, at which point you designate up to 10 willing creatures within 20 feet of you. After spending a minute concentrating on the smoke and its scent, you and the affected creatures move into the [Netherworld](/Planes.aspx?ID=36) and can use its warped nature to speed travel. Each hour, your travel covers a distance of 50 miles, during which landmarks appear as vague and symbolic images rather than concrete visuals. You arrive within a mile of your intended destination when you [Dismiss](/Actions.aspx?ID=2311) the effect or after 8 hours have passed.

_Nevercold_, sometimes mistakenly referred to as nevercoal, is the charcoal left after wildfires in the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=10). True to its name, _nevercold_ remains warm to the touch. If you use _nevercold_ to cast [_fire shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=118), the spell's duration increases by 5 minutes, the cold resistance you gain from it lasts 1 hour, and you're protected from the effects of [severe cold](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) for 8 hours.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Wake the Dead #1](/Sources.aspx?ID=201) pg. 26

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Longsword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

More often called by their nickname “screamswords,” the Nexian sealing blades were developed by the Arclords of Nex as special tools to ward off Gebbite infiltrators and assassins. Screamswords are _+1 striking [disrupting](/Equipment.aspx?ID=294) [silver](/Equipment.aspx?ID=277) [longswords](/Weapons.aspx?ID=31)_ with a couple of extra tricks. Each Nexian sealing blade can sense undead within 60 feet and responds by screaming loudly until there are no longer undead within that range. This same screaming can be unleashed as a sonic blast if needed. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** the screamsword does what it does best and lets out an ear-shattering shriek. Each creature in a 30-foot cone takes 6d6 sonic damage (DC 25 basic Fortitude save). Any creature who fails is [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 1 round, or 1 hour on a critical failure

Each Nexian sealing blade can sense undead within 60 feet and responds by screaming loudly until there are no longer undead within that range. This same screaming can be unleashed as a sonic blast if needed. 

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact;  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** the screamsword does what it does best and lets out an ear-shattering shriek. <title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Nightbreeze Machine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1154)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Air" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=5" />
<trait label="Clockwork" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=331" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 88

_[**PFS Note**](/pathfinder-society) All Pathfinder Society agents have access to all uncommon clockwork items and gadgets from Chapters 1 and 2 of this book_

**Price** 125 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 4
</row>

**Access** Characters from Absalom, New Thassilon, Alkenstar, Dongun Hold, or especially technological regions of Arcadia like the Deadshot Lands have access to uncommon clockwork items from the first two chapters of this book.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The nightbreeze machine can turn a scorching hot room into a comfortable one with just the pull of a lever. Its outer shell is a brass cube half as tall as the average human that houses a series of flat metal “blades” in a circular arrangement. When placed on a flat surface, a creature within reach can Interact to flip the lever, turning the machine on. When the machine is active, the blades begin to spin rapidly, setting the air in the room into motion, which cools off the room's inhabitants. A front-mounted metal grate prevents anyone from coming into accidental contact with the spinning blades without impeding airflow.

 The nightbreeze machine was recently commissioned by Malduoni, Keeper of the First Law, leader of the nation of Rahadoum. He tasked the country's brightest inventors with creating devices that would, in his words, “Ensure that no mortal need fear death from the desert heat.” This machine was the first creation to come out of this consolidated engineering effort, but it won't be the last.

 A nightbreeze machine can affect an enclosed area of no more than 50 feet by 50 feet and has negligible effect when used in a larger enclosed area or outside. While active, it reduces the effects of [severe heat](/Rules.aspx?ID=642) by one step to mild heat, and reduces extreme heat to severe heat. A nightbreeze machine isn't powerful enough to reduce the effects of incredible heat, though fortunately such heat isn't found naturally in the deserts of Rahadoum. A nightbreeze machine runs for 8 hours, after which it must be wound in a process that takes 10 minutes to complete. The 8 hours of activity don't have to be consecutive.

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 9"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Nightmare](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3453)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Seven Dooms for Sandpoint</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 185

**Price** 250 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** etched onto a weapon

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

A _nightmare_ rune creates minor phantasmal alterations to a weapon's appearance so that those who look upon it see subtle reminders of their deepest fears. An arachnophobe might interpret the cross guard of a _nightmare_ longsword to look like curving, twitching spider legs, for example, while someone who's afraid of sickness might see a _nightmare_ club as a diseased length of bone crawling with flies. These images are all in the mind of the observer, but they also infuse the weapon with additional power. When you hit with a nightmare weapon, add 1d6 mental damage to the damage dealt. In addition, on a critical hit, the target becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 by overwhelming visions in their mind of personal horrors that linger. If you critically hit a creature that's already stupefied, it becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 2 as well. These critical hit effects have the [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=590), [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=598), and [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) traits. 

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision, Interact);  **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** The _nightmare weapon_ casts [_nightmare_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1615) to your specifications.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 11"
    pfs=""
>
[Nightmare Cudgel](/Equipment.aspx?ID=890)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Agents of Edgewatch</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #161: Belly of the Black Whale](/Sources.aspx?ID=51) pg. 78

**Price** 1,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Crafted from polished wood, this seemingly mundane _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [club](/Weapons.aspx?ID=2)_ comes with a red leather strap near the handle. The mere sight of the cudgel in a guard's hand fills prisoners with dread. Good creatures are [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) while carrying, wielding, or wearing this item crafted by the sea-witches.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You initiate an intimidating walk, thumping the cudgel menacingly against your palm. As part of activating this item, you can Stride twice. For the next minute, whenever you successfully Strike a creature with the _nightmare cudgel_, you can use a free action to attempt an [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) the struck creature.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Ritually constructed from the bones of a [nightmare](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3105), a _nightmare’s lament_ is a _[+1](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2830) [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2829) [rapier pistol](/Weapons.aspx?ID=222)_. Thin wisps of dark smoke continually surround the redflecked blade.

**Activate—Fuming Cloak** <actions string="Two Actions" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** For 1 minute, the _nightmare’s lament_ continually vents thick, black smoke that creates [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=62) in a 15-foot aura around the gun’s wielder. The wielder of the nightmare’s lament can see through this smoke. A creature that begins its turn in the area becomes [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 2 (DC 23 Fortitude negates) and is then temporarily immune to the sickness from the smoke for 1 minute. The wielder of the _nightmare’s lament_, any creature currently holding its breath (or that does not need to breathe), and any creature immune to poison are immune to the aura’s sickened effect but not the concealment.

**Craft Requirements** The initial raw materials must include the rib bones and inner fire of a [nightmare](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3105).

<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The [dwarves](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=1) of Cloudspire Citadel in Golarion's Mwangi Expanse create bottles of _nimbus breath_ by capturing and bottling the fluffiest nimbus clouds from the lairs of cloud dragons. After harvesting the cloud, the bottle must sit at the peak of the tallest mountain for 10 days and 10 nights, pelted by all forms of weather. _Nimbus breaths_ can also be created by capturing clouds on other planes, such as those found on the [Plane of Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4) or in the highest peaks of Celestia.

 After you inhale the _nimbus breath_, you gain resistance 5 to electricity and are affected by [_fly_](/Spells.aspx?ID=125) as long as you hold your breath.  You can exhale the breath as a single action to create a [_gust of wind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=143) (DC 24) from your mouth. If you're airborne when the cloud expires, you float gently to the ground at 60 feet per round and don't take damage from this fall.

The ink on these tattoos, made from the crushed crystalline fangs and wingbones of sceaduinars, lends a dull purple-black hue to your arms and hands. During combat, the ink moves of its own accord, coalescing into nine smoky crystal spurs of darkness; these eerie finger-like protrusions move with an unearthly grace on your command, supplying the requisite magical gestures for your spells. 

**Activate—Shadow Fingers** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=561), shadow, [spellshape](/Traits.aspx?ID=513)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes;   **Effect** If your next action is to [Cast a Spell](/Actions.aspx?ID=2734) with the [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) trait, your spell loses the [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645) trait and gains the shadow trait, as the tattoo’s shadowy spurs perform the gestures in your stead.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Season of Ghosts</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #196: The Summer That Never Was](/Sources.aspx?ID=214) pg. 82

**Price** 85 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn helmet

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This unpleasant-looking hood appears to be a completely smooth, round sack of skin that feels uncannily warm to the touch. When you wear this hood and invest it, it merges with your head and face, becoming imperceptible as a worn item except on close examination, which reveals a slight oily sheen to your facial features. You can cause minor shifts and changes to your features while wearing a _noppera-bo hood_; this counts as having a [disguise kit](/Equipment.aspx?ID=19) to [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) any creature that is the same ancestry as you.

**Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> envision ([transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** You focus on the hood's magic, and then gain the effects of 1st-level [_illusory disguise_](/Spells.aspx?ID=159), though it's a [transmutation](/Traits.aspx?ID=157) effect rather than an [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92).

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 99 --- Light and strong, noqual also demonstrates a powerful resistance to magic. A side effect of this resistance is that making magical weapons out of noqual requires complex and expensive alchemical treatments. Kevoth-Kul, the Black Sovereign of Numeria, has developed an alloy of noqual and cold iron known as [sovereign steel](/Equipment.aspx?ID=776) to help mitigate this property. The metal's crystalline appearance might suggest that it's fragile, but the pale-green material can be worked similarly to iron. Objects made of noqual have a +4 circumstance bonus on saves against magic that the item attempts and grant their bonus to saves the owner makes specifically to protect the item from magic (such as against the [_rusting grasp_](/Spells.aspx?ID=711) spell). ## Noqual

Noqual shields are notoriously difficult to make, requiring high-grade materials, but they're especially effective against magic. When you have a noqual shield [Raised](/Actions.aspx?ID=98), you gain its circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells that target you (as well as AC). Additionally, while the shield is Raised, when an opponent casting a spell that targets you critically fails a spell attack roll against your AC, you can reflect the spell back toward them as a reaction. Attempt a ranged attack roll against the triggering creature using your highest proficiency with a ranged weapon. If you succeed, your opponent takes the effects of a successful spell attack roll for their own spell (or the effects of a critical success if your attack roll was a critical success).

[North Wind's Night Verse](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1068)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Cold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=27" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 187

**Price** 900 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Katana](/Weapons.aspx?ID=55)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [frost](/Equipment.aspx?ID=296) [katana](/Weapons.aspx?ID=55)_ is always cool to the touch, nearly uncomfortably so. Unadorned and with no tsuba, its honed blade is carved from a single tusk of [dragon-turtle](/Monsters.aspx?ID=157) ivory and wrapped in strips of [winter wolf](/Monsters.aspx?ID=403) hide. Strikes with the katana gain a +2 status bonus to damage rolls against creatures that have a status penalty to their Speed or are [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35). The status bonus increases to +3 if the weapon has a _greater striking rune_ and +4 for _major striking_.

**Activate** <actions string="Free Action" /> command ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), [evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)) **Frequency** once per 1 minute; **Trigger** Your spell deals cold damage to a creature;  **Effect** Choose one creature dealt cold damage by the spell. It takes a –5-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

    right="Item 12+"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Nosoi Charm](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1095)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Night of the Gray Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99) pg. 53

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Nosois serve as scribes and messengers to psychopomps. They are rare outside of the Boneyard, so it's common for [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) venturing to other planes to carry a nosoi facsimile to aid in their travels. This tiny icon of a masked raven emits twittering sounds in perfect accompaniment to your performances. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play an instrument, orate, or sing. You can cast [_sending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) once per day as a divine innate spell. 

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You twist the base of the charm, and the twittering it emits becomes helpful words to boost your arguments. You lose the item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks and gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to make [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) until you use this activation again.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You gain [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21) as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour as long as you continue to hold the charm. This allows you to sense the life force that animates living creatures and the perverse force that animates the dead, though you can't distinguish between the two.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Night of the Gray Death</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99) pg. 53

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Nosois serve as scribes and messengers to psychopomps. They are rare outside of the Boneyard, so it's common for [psychopomps](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) venturing to other planes to carry a nosoi facsimile to aid in their travels. This tiny icon of a masked raven emits twittering sounds in perfect accompaniment to your performances. You gain a +2 item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks to play an instrument, orate, or sing. You can cast [_sending_](/Spells.aspx?ID=272) once per day as a divine innate spell. 

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> Interact;     **Effect** You twist the base of the charm, and the twittering it emits becomes helpful words to boost your arguments. You lose the item bonus to [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) checks and gain a +2 item bonus to [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) checks to make [Requests](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) until you use this activation again.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;     **Effect** You gain [lifesense](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=21) as an imprecise sense with a range of 30 feet for 1 hour as long as you continue to hold the charm. This allows you to sense the life force that animates living creatures and the perverse force that animates the dead, though you can't distinguish between the two.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Catalyst" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=396" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Secrets of Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=96) pg. 169

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="" /><row>Cast a Spell</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

---

Sold only in single sticks, this foul incense comes coated with a bevy of alchemical smoke that activates in the presence of intense heat, releasing its namesake pungent odor. Adding this catalyst to a [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362) spell fills all squares adjacent to the wall with thick, foul smoke. Creatures in this area are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4), and other creatures are concealed to creatures in the area. The smoke lasts for the duration of the spell.

May contain spoilers from Extinction Curse **Source** [Pathfinder #154: Siege of the Dinosaurs](/Sources.aspx?ID=31) pg. 76 **Price** 2,800 gp **Usage** worn **Bulk** L **Base Armor** [Padded Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=3) --- This _+2 resilient [padded armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=3)_ is woven from many strands of gut cord strung with dried organs and preserved [xulgath](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=102) scent glands. When worn, it infuses your body with a ghastly and nauseating flavor. **Activate** envision; **Trigger** You are grabbed or are hit by an unarmed attack; **Effect** Your attacker must attempt a DC 28 Fortitude saving throw. Creatures with a stench aura, such as [otyughs](/Monsters.aspx?ID=327) and xulgaths, are immune to this effect. **Success** The creature is unaffected and is immune to the effects of the noxious jerkin for 1 minute.
**Failure** The creature is [sickened 1.](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34)
**Critical Failure** The creature is sickened 1 and is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 round.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 602

**Price** 1,300 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Composite Longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=74)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Constructed of a flexible, white wood and with ornate, twisting designs carved into its surface, this _+2 striking composite [longbow](/Weapons.aspx?ID=76)_ appears to have been made by [elves](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=2). Sometimes when you loose an arrow, its whistling in flight sounds like a voice whispering in [Elven](/Languages.aspx?ID=4), wishing for the swift defeat of your enemies.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> command;     **Effect** You swear an oath to destroy one creature you can see. For the next 7 days or until that creature is slain, your attacks with the bow against that creature deal 1d6 additional damage, and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) checks to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) that creature. Your critical hits against the target gain the bow’s critical specialization effect; if they would already do so, they instead increase the DC of the [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) when critically hit to DC 20.

After you activate the bow, you can’t activate it again for 7 days. If you kill the creature you’ve sworn an oath against, the oath ends and you need to wait only 10 minutes before you can activate it again.

</column>

This hooded lantern takes the form of a translucent prism. It functions as a normal [hooded lantern](/Equipment.aspx?ID=2730), except that it isn’t fueled by oil, but by oaths. While you’re holding the lantern, you gain a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks.

**Activate—Annouce Oath** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([light](/Traits.aspx?ID=640), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647))  **Trigger** You make a promise in good faith;  **Effect** The _oathlamp of accord_ sheds light without consuming fuel until the promise you made is broken or fulfilled. The GM adjudicates whether a spoken promise is broken or fulfilled. This light and the shutters to conceal it work as normal for a hooded lantern. Any creature in the light of the oathlamp becomes aware of the contents of the oath, along with who made it and how long ago.

You can spread this blue-gray gel on a single item with a Bulk of 3 or less to ward it against magical detection. It becomes undetectable to detection, revelation, and scrying magic of 8th rank or lower (such as [_locate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=173)). This oil is permanent, but it can be removed with acid. Removing the oil in this way usually takes 1 minute for objects with Bulk of 1 or less, or a number of minutes equal to the item's Bulk.

**Bulk** 2
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Weapon** [Gun Sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=218)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This black obsidian blade is a _+1 [striking](/Equipment.aspx?ID=280) [gun sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=218)_. Magma seeps along its many cracks and crags, and the handle is hot but not scalding to the touch. Strikes with this gun sword deal 1 extra fire damage.

**Activate—Explosion of Shards** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes;  **Requirements** Your most recent action this turn was a successful ranged Strike with _obsidian edge_; **Effect** Magma coats the sword blade completely before exploding from your weapon in a 15-foot emanation of fire and glass. Creatures in the area take 2d6 fire damage and 2d6 piercing damage with a DC 20 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Item 5+"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Obsidian Goggles](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3097)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=637" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 293

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn eyepiece

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The sleek, black lenses of these goggles somehow make everything seem more brightly lit. While wearing the goggles, you gain a +1 item bonus to Perception checks involving sight. 

**Activate—Darkvision** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Frequency** once per day;   **Effect** Adjusting your goggles, you gain darkvision for 1 hour. 

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 5"
pfs="Standard"
>
Obsidian Goggles
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 11"
pfs="Standard"
>
Obsidian Goggles (Greater)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 293

**Price** 1,250 gp

<row gap="medium">

</row>

</column>

---

The item bonus is +2, the goggles can be activated any number of times per day, and the activation lasts until you deactivate it as an Interact action or the item is no longer invested by you, whichever comes first.

pfs="Standard"

</title>

**Usage** held in 1 hand

</row>

**Access** A character who is a member of the Pathfinder Society has access to this option.

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

The four different types of _scroll cases of simplicity_ often bear adornments appropriate to their magical tradition, such as angelic wings or otherworldly lettering. On the inside, intricate runic diagrams spiral out to surround the scroll stored within. A scroll placed within the case can be converted into energy to cast consistently useful spells depending on its type. You must be able to cast spells of a given tradition to use a _scroll case of simplicity_ of a corresponding type.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> Interact;    **Requirements** The scroll case contains a single scroll of a 1st-level spell; **Effect** You transfer the scroll’s energy into the scroll case, consuming the scroll, and you can immediately begin casting one of the scroll case’s spells. If you use any action other than to Cast a Spell from the scroll case after activating the _scroll case of simplicity_, the scroll and its energy are lost.

    right="Item 9+"
    pfs=""
>
[Fulcrum Lenses](/Equipment.aspx?ID=942)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 75

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

_Fulcrum lenses_ are unique magical crystals that each contain a sliver of [Nhimbaloth's](/Deities.aspx?ID=163) essence. They belong to a larger set of lenses created to manipulate or even bind the Empty Death; most of the other lenses are long lost and likely destroyed. The Haruvex family came into possession of four of the lenses, and they knew that bringing them together focused Nhimbaloth's attention in unprecedented and dangerous ways. Belcorra brought all four lenses to the Abomination Vaults with her, intending to install them in Gauntlight for her ultimate revenge upon Absalom. She also created a special receptacle called the [_Fulcrum Lattice_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=943) to hold the lenses so that their power could be focused together. She realized the danger of keeping the _fulcrum lenses_ too close together until the right time and spread them out among loyal groups in the Abomination Vaults' lowest levels for safekeeping.

 Belcorra keeps only the most powerful lens, the _Ebon Fulcrum Lens_, with her—indeed, as a ghost, it's the only one she can carry. If the heroes can bring the other three lenses to bear against Belcorra, they can draw Nhimbaloth's dread glare to the sorcerer. Despite her loyalty, Belcorra can't hope to keep her spirit intact when Nhimbaloth gazes directly upon it.

 The _fulcrum lenses_ are more than mere receptacles of Nhimbaloth's essence. Each grants those who use it a fragment of the Great Old One's power.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

<title
level="2"
right="Item 9"
pfs=""
>
Crimson Fulcrum Lens
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Abomination Vaults</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 75

**Price** 700 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 1

</row>

</column>

---

This concave lens has a drifting crimson cloud resembling slowly swirling blood within it. While you have the _Crimson Fulcrum Lens_ invested, you seethe with malevolent fury you can barely contain. You gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) effects and a +2 item bonus to your melee [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=89) damage (this increases to a +4 item bonus to damage if the melee Strike is a jaws attack). You can also activate the lens in the following ways. 

 **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You grasp the Crimson Fulcrum Lens in one hand and make a Strike that doesn't require that hand. The Strike deals an additional 1d8 precision damage (or 2d8 precision damage if you make a jaws Strike) and doesn't count toward your multiple attack penalty. 

 **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15), [possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=129)); **Effect** While grasping the lens, make a melee spell attack roll with a modifier of +18. On a hit, you force the splinter of Nhimbaloth's essence from the lens to possess the target. You're no longer invested in the lens, and the target gains the benefits as though it had invested the lens but can't activate the lens's other abilities. This effect is permanent, but it can be ended by any effect that removes a possession effect. The lens doesn't have any magical abilities until the possession effect ends; when it does, the essence returns to the lens.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 12"
pfs=""
>
Ebon Fulcrum Lens
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Abomination Vaults</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 75

**Price** 2,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L

</row>

</column>

---

This strangest and most powerful of the fulcrum lenses resembles a chip of smooth obsidian containing three dark glimmers of Nhimbaloth's essence. Incorporeal creatures can touch and hold the _Ebon Fulcrum Lens_. While you have the _Ebon Fulcrum Lens_ invested, and you're a corporeal creature, you become insubstantial, gain the incorporeal trait, and are [drained 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10). Your drained condition can't be reduced below 2 as long as you have the lens invested. You can activate the lens in the following ways. Both require expenditures of glimmers within the lens; once the lens is depleted of its three glimmers, it retains its ability to make corporeal creatures insubstantial but can't be used for its other abilities until its glimmers are restored (which generally requires a ritual or being steeped in an area of Nhimbaloth's power). 

 **Activate** <actions string="Reaction" /> envision; **Frequency** once per day; **Requirement** At least one glimmer remains in the _Ebon Fulcrum Lens_; **Prerequisites** you have the rejuvenation ability; **Trigger** you would be destroyed and are able to rejuvenate; **Effect** For the first 24 hours after you rejuvenate, you gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and DCs. Reduce the number of glimmers remaining in the lens by 1. 

 **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Requirement** At least one glimmer remains in the _Ebon Fulcrum Lens_; **Effect** You draw upon a glimmer of Nhimbaloth's essence for power; reduce the number of glimmers remaining in the lens by 1. You're [quickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=32) for 1 minute and gain a +1 item bonus to attack rolls, saving throws, and DCs. You can use this extra action to [Stride](/Actions.aspx?ID=88) or [Step](/Actions.aspx?ID=87), or for an action in a special ghost ability you have.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 10"
pfs=""
>
Emerald Fulcrum Lens
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Abomination Vaults</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Negative" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=118" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 75

**Price** 1,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 3

</row>

</column>

---

This concave green lens is pitted and flawed; its jagged edges can cut those who don't handle it with care. While you have the _Emerald Fulcrum Lens_ invested, your flesh appears waxen and pallid. You gain [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42) and [_harm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=146) spells gain a +4 status bonus to the Hit Points they restore to you. You can also activate the lens in the following ways. 

 **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([healing](/Traits.aspx?ID=89)); **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You grasp the _Emerald Fulcrum Lens_ in one hand, regain 30 Hit Points, and gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against magic for 1 round. 

 **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15), [possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=129)); **Effect** While grasping the lens, make a melee spell attack roll with a modifier of +20. On a hit, you force the splinter of Nhimbaloth's essence from the lens to possess the target. You're no longer invested in the lens, and the target gains the benefits as though it had invested the lens but can't activate the lens's other abilities. This effect is permanent, but it can be ended by any effect that removes a possession effect. The lens doesn't have any magical abilities until the possession effect ends; when it does, the essence returns to the lens.

<title
level="2"
right="Item 11"
pfs=""
>
Ochre Fulcrum Lens
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Abomination Vaults</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Invested" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=98" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 75

**Price** 1,400 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 2

</row>

</column>

---

This brownish-orange lens always seems dusty and gritty, even when wet. While you have the _Ochre Fulcrum Lens_ invested, lassitude grips you. You gain resistance 10 to [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) damage and a +2 status bonus to saves against [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60) effects. You can also activate the lens in the following ways. 

 **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact; **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You hold up the _Ochre Fulcrum Lens_ in your hand and the item casts [_crushing despair_](/Spells.aspx?ID=57) (DC 31 Will save). 

 **Activate** <actions string="Two Actions" /> Interact ([attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15), [possession](/Traits.aspx?ID=129)); **Effect** While grasping the lens, make a melee spell attack roll with a modifier of +21. On a hit, you force the splinter of Nhimbaloth's essence from the lens to possess the target. You're no longer invested in the lens, and the target gains the benefits as though it had invested the lens but can't activate the lens's other abilities. This effect is permanent, but it can be ended by any effect that removes a possession effect. The lens doesn't have any magical abilities until the possession effect ends; when it does, the essence returns to the lens.

**Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 178 **Usage** held in 1 hand **Bulk** L **Activate**([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) --- Eight flailing octopus arms covered in suckers pop out from the sides of your body when you imbibe this potion. The arms share your multiple attack penalty and attempt to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) a random enemy within 15 feet of you. On a success, roll 1d4 to determine an additional effect of the arms, which lasts as long as the target remains grabbed or restrained by the arms. On subsequent turns, you can use a single action, which has the [attack](/Traits.aspx?ID=15) trait, to have the arms either Grapple a creature currently [grappled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) (with no added effect) or release any creature they currently hold and repeat their initial effect. After 1 minute, the arms disappear and the potion's effects end.
**1d4****Added Effect**
1The arms cover the eyes; the target is also [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=1).
2The arms cover the mouth; the target can't speak.
3The arms wrap around the limbs; the flat check for the target to use a [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) action while grabbed is DC 7 instead of DC 5.
4 The arms crush your enemy; the target takes bludgeoning damage equal to the potion's level immediately and at the end of each of its turns.
Octopus Potion (Lesser) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 178 **Price** 50 gp **Bulk** L --- The Athletics modifier is +12 and the [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC is 20. Octopus Potion (Moderate) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 178 **Price** 130 gp **Bulk** L --- The Athletics modifier is +17 and the Escape DC is 25. Octopus Potion (Greater) **Source** [Rage of Elements](/Sources.aspx?ID=205) pg. 178 **Price** 500 gp **Bulk** L --- The Athletics modifier is +22 and the Escape DC is 30.

>
[Oculus of Abaddon](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1747)
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Kingmaker</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Artifact" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=253" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Evil" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=64" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 587

<row gap="medium">

</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

An _oculus of Abaddon_ is a potent artifact rumored to have been created by one of the [Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=11) as a way to reward those who work as their agents on the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1). More likely, these items were crafted by a powerful pre-Earthfall death cult that has long since moved on, leaving behind these dangerous artifacts to tempt mortals into serving the needs of the Horsemen. 

An _oculus of Abaddon_ appears as a sphere of clear crystal that contains a pinpoint of flickering red light at its center. When held, the oculus feels warm to the touch and fills you with a sudden desire to pluck out an eye and place the oculus within the socket—this causes 4d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). Once placed in an eye socket, the oculus can be removed only by ripping it free (causing the same amount of persistent bleed damage as the initial plucking). When you place the oculus in your empty eye socket, you immediately heal all damage caused by plucking the previous eye out. Once placed, an oculus grants you constant [darkvision](/Rules.aspx?ID=415). It can also be activated to perform a number of other magical effects, as detailed below, but if you aren't evil, each time you activate an _oculus of Abaddon_, you must succeed at a DC 36 Will save or become affected by a [_subconscious suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=314) (heightened to 8th level) to perform an evil act the next time an opportunity to do so arises, as determined by the GM.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 10 minutes (envision);  **Frequency** three times per day;   **Effect** You gain the effects of [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268), heightened to 7th level.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Cast a Spell;  **Frequency** once per week;   **Effect** You use the _oculus of Abaddon_ to cast a [_planar binding_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=17) ritual, heightened to 7th level. You can only conjure neutral evil creatures with this casting of _planar binding_. If you already know the _planar binding_ ritual, you gain a +3 item bonus on the primary check when casting _planar binding_.

**Activate** <actions string="Three Actions" /> envision;    **Requirements** you have a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=160) or [animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=149); **Effect** You can see and hear through your familiar or animal companion's eyes and ears, provided you are on the same plane. This effect can be sustained, but as long as you do so you can take no other actions.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> 1 hour (envision; [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64)) **Frequency** once per year;   **Effect** You manipulate the minds of a huge number of targets, provided that the end goal of the manipulation is a tragic or otherwise horrific fate for those being manipulated. This functions as [_suggestion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=315), but with a range of 1 mile. All creatures within this area are affected, with the same suggestion implanted in their minds. Creatures hear the telepathic suggestion in their native language, and creatures that are 7th level or higher can attempt a DC 36 Will save to resist the effect. This power was used by Vordakai to cause the vanishing of Varnhold, suggesting to its inhabitants to leave their homes and travel south to his tomb. If this effect is [counteracted](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) or removed on one victim, it ends for all victims.

**Destruction** A foul and hideous object, an _oculus of Abaddon_ is fortunately relatively easy to destroy, as far as artifacts go. It has Hardness 25 and 100 Hit Points, but repairs damage to itself swiftly, regaining 10 Hit Points per round. It has weakness 10 to bludgeoning damage and weakness 30 to good damage.

Adlet spiritual leaders create this thick purple gel so that the dead can temporarily assume their appearance in life during ancestral worship ceremonies. Spreading it over the bones of an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature or a lifeless corpse causes the gel to congeal, forming a cosmetic layer that covers or restores any missing or compromised flesh until the body mimics its appearance in life. The dead creature's flesh looks healthy and whole. It gains a +2 circumstance bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks to look like a living creature. The gel does not restore life or Hit Points and the flesh quickly rots away 8 hours after application.

Spreading it over the bones of an undead creature or a lifeless corpse causes the gel to congeal, forming a cosmetic layer that covers or restores any missing or compromised flesh until the body mimics its appearance in life. The dead creature’s flesh looks healthy and whole. An undead creature covered with the oil gains a +2 circumstance bonus on [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) checks to look like a living creature. The gel does not restore life or Hit Points and the flesh quickly rots away 8 hours after application.

This fine golden oil comes in a small blue canister. Carefully spreading the oil over an object turns it into an [animated object](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=4) of the same type. For example, sprinkling it on a statue makes an [animated statue](/Monsters.aspx?ID=20). If the animated object's level would be greater than 3, the oil struggles to animate it and ultimately fails.

 This animated object has the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) trait, meaning it can use 2 actions when you Command it. You can issue a Command for the current turn as part of the activation. The object remains animated for 1 minute before falling inert. As usual, you can have a maximum of four minions under your control.

---

This thin, slippery oil shimmers with a golden hue. Coating your shoes or feet with _oil of skating_ enables you to skate quickly along flat surfaces for 1 hour. You gain a +10-foot status bonus to your Speed, which doubles if you move on a downhill surface. You lose this bonus if moving on difficult terrain, greater difficult terrain, or [uneven ground](/Rules.aspx?ID=456). Also, you treat any uphill movement as moving on difficult terrain while your feet are oiled and treat the results of any [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) checks made to [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=28) as one degree worse.

[Oilskin Pouch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3249)
</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 113

**Price** 5 sp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Treated with oil and animal fats, the leather of this pouch is more resistant to water but is also stiffer. Many makers and travelers decorate their oilskin pouches with symbols of the ocean and sailing. Often used to store scrolls or other paper documents when a traveler knows they will be in an area of heavy rain or near water. While not entirely waterproof, an oilskin pouch seals with sturdy leather ties, allowing it to resist anything other than total submersion. Even completely underwater, it will protect its contents for up to 1 minute. 

An oilskin pouch can protect up to 1 Bulk of items.

A thin sheen of slick oil covers this gaudy button.     level="1"
    right="Item 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Old Tillimaquin](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1617)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Enchantment" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=61" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 63

**Price** 2,000 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Bulk** 3
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This beloved tavern mascot is a shabby old stuffed beast mounted on an immense slab of ironwood. The beast is roughly the size and shape of a wolverine but with a broader snout, blue stripes along its upper legs and bristled back, and a club of spiked bone at the end of its long tail. No one can recall where _Old Tillimaquin_ originally came from, how the taxidermic beast came to stand in its tavern, or even whether it's a genuine article. The tradition of rubbing its bronzed claws for good luck has been observed for so long that the front claws are worn to stubs. Local belief holds that as long as _Old Tillimaquin_ stands, neither fire nor flood will claim its town.

**Activate** <actions string="" /> Interact ([divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Frequency** once per month;   **Effect** You rub _Old Tillimaquin's_ bronzed claws for good luck before setting out on a task that might benefit the town. You can reroll a single failed saving throw within the next 24 hours, but you must take the second result, even if it's worse than your original result. Each person who rubs the claws can benefit only once per month, but there's no limit to how many people can draw on _Old Tillimaquin's_ luck.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

[Olfactory Obfuscator](/Equipment.aspx?ID=690)
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=59" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Advanced Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=39) pg. 254

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This frothing fluid causes the drinker's body to exude trace odor-absorbing oils. For the listed duration after drinking this elixir, your scent is nearly unnoticeable. Creatures with imprecise scent don't detect you with that sense unless they [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) for you, and you are [concealed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from creatures that perceive you with precise scent. You gain a +4 item bonus against attempts to Seek you by creatures using only scent-based senses; if they use any other senses as well, the bonus doesn't apply.

---

This cluster of sensitive wire whiskers fits over the nose or snout to provide sensory information as it reacts to nearby odors and other scents. A creature wearing _olfactory stimulators_ gains a sense of smell, which is as precise as an average member of its species, as well as the [scent](/Rules.aspx?ID=417) special ability if members of its species typically have that ability. _Olfactory stimulators_ can be fitted to animal companions as well as sapient creatures; stimulators produced for companion use have the [companion](/Traits.aspx?ID=29) trait.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=721" />
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=528" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=564" />
<trait label="Elixir" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=589" />
<trait label="Mutagen" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=116" />
<trait label="Polymorph" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=670" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Howl of the Wild](/Sources.aspx?ID=226) pg. 110

**Price** 65 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** held in 1 hand

**Bulk** L
</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))</row></row>

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

Your eyes bulge from their sockets and extend upwards from your head on long, prehensile stalks, greatly enhancing your eyesight and field of view but leaving you unable to close your eyes, increasing your vulnerability to harmful visual effects.

**Benefit** You gain [all-around vision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=49), a +2 item bonus to visual [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298) checks, and [low-light vision](/Rules.aspx?ID=2411) if you don’t already have it. These effects last for 1 minute.

**Drawback** For 1 minute, you take a –2 penalty to saving throws against effects that have the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=727) trait.

---

This glass bottle holds breezes captured from the heart of the Plane of Air. When you inhale the bottle’s contents, the air fills your lungs so completely that you no longer need to breathe, at least for a time. While the effect lasts, you also gain a status bonus against inhaled threats, such as inhaled poisons. If you spend 1 [Mythic Point](/Rules.aspx?ID=3323) when you activate the _day’s breath_, you inhale so deeply that you increase the effect’s duration.

---

One hundred cuts, healed into diamond-shaped scars, represent the ability to withstand the attacks of your enemies. [Orc](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=19) warriors covet these scar patterns and cluster them around what they consider to be their strongest assets—a pattern around the heart signifies a warrior with great endurance, while one along the arms indicates great upper body strength. 

You gain a +1 item bonus to [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) checks. If you have [Ferocity](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=16) (such as from the [Orc Ferocity](/Feats.aspx?ID=83) feat or a similar ability), the first time each day you use it, instead of remaining at 1 Hit Point, your Hit Points are set to an amount equal to your ancestry Hit Points, even if this amount is more than you had before using Ferocity.

</column>

---

Popular with lovers, decorators, and sports fans, the seeds of these ephemeral plants grow and bloom immediately into flowers when placed in any warm environment, including a cup of dirt, a bowl of warm water, and a tightly clenched hand. The color of these flowers varies, but each has an internal glow that sheds [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2401) in a 30-foot radius. The radius of this light shrinks by 10 feet every 20 minutes. At the end of an hour, the plant disintegrates, leaving only a vaguely pleasant scent in the air.

---

Ooze ammunition is a capsule containing a sticky substance. If you hit a creature with activated ooze ammunition, it deals acid damage instead of its normal damage type, and the creature then takes the listed penalty to Speed and [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) until it ends the effects. On a critical hit, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) for 1 round in addition to the other effects. The target can end the effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) the sticky foam. Other creatures can provide the actions, although doing so deals half the ammunition's persistent acid damage to the assisting creature. A creature that ends the effect still takes the persistent damage that turn.

Ooze ammunition is a capsule containing a sticky substance. If you hit a creature with activated ooze ammunition, it deals acid damage instead of its normal damage type, and the creature then takes the listed penalty to Speed and persistent acid damage until it ends the effects. On a critical hit, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) for 1 round in addition to the other effects. The target can end the effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) the sticky foam. Other creatures can provide the actions, although doing so deals half the ammunition’s [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) to the assisting creature. A creature that ends the effect still takes the persistent damage that turn.

</title>

<traits>

<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
<trait label="Consumable" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=36" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault](/Sources.aspx?ID=320) pg. 43

</row>

<row gap="medium">
<row gap="tiny"><row>**Activate**</row><actions string="Single Action" /><row>Interact</row></row>

---

Ooze ammunition is a capsule containing a sticky substance. If you hit a creature with activated ooze ammunition, it deals acid damage instead of its normal damage type, and the creature then takes the listed penalty to Speed and persistent acid damage until it ends the effects. On a critical hit, the creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) for 1 round in addition to the other effects. The target can end the effects by [Escaping](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) the sticky foam. Other creatures can provide the actions, although doing so deals half the ammunition’s [persistent acid damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) to the assisting creature. A creature that ends the effect still takes the persistent damage that turn.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Alchemical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=6" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Treasure Vault (Remastered)](/Sources.aspx?ID=191) pg. 64

**Price** 150 gp

<row gap="medium">

**Usage** worn armor

**Bulk** 1
</row>

<row gap="medium">
**Base Armor** [Leather Armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41)
</row>

<row gap="medium">

 

 

 
</row>

</column>

---

This [leather armor](/Armor.aspx?ID=41) has been treated with extract from [oozes](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=453), which can be reactivated in the presence of a strong acid. A receptacle in the armor can hold an [acid flask](/Equipment.aspx?ID=3286), which takes 3 Interact actions to install.

**Activate** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=645))   **Requirements** An acid flask is installed in the armor; **Effect** The leather weeps slippery protoplasm, granting an item bonus to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) and [Squeeze](/Actions.aspx?ID=2372) checks equal to the acid flask’s item bonus. The protoplasm also irritates the skin on prolonged contact, causing any creature that [grapples](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) or [swallows](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=77) you to take acid damage equal to the acid flask’s splash damage. Ooze skin remains activated for a number of rounds equal to the level of the acid flask installed. The activation uses up the acid flask, and the armor can’t be activated again until a new one is installed.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>
